correct.A: Queries filter by department before ranking, so B-tree indexes on the filtered columns narrow the candidate rows first and cut CPU work.

incorrect.B: Storing embeddings as JSON removes the native vector type and makes similarity search slower.
incorrect.C: Higher dimensionality makes every distance calculation more expensive.
incorrect.D: A longer statement timeout hides slow queries; it does not speed them up.

correct.D: Limiting the result count (for example TOP 5 ordered by VectorDistance) returns just the five most similar documents.

incorrect.A: Offset pagination skips rows; it does not select the nearest ones.
incorrect.B: Consistency level controls read guarantees, not which documents match.
incorrect.C: Grouping by an embedding value is meaningless for similarity ranking.

correct.A: Always Encrypted starts with a customer-managed key in Azure Key Vault; the data encryption keys are then protected by it.

incorrect.B: The data encryption key must be wrapped by the CMK, so the CMK has to exist first.
incorrect.C: A managed identity can access the vault later, but it is not the first step.
incorrect.D: The container encryption policy references the keys, so the keys must exist first.

correct.B: Deleting related cache keys when the source changes guarantees stale entries are never returned.
correct.D: A 10-minute TTL on each key makes results expire after exactly the required time.

incorrect.A: Keyspace notifications only notify about events; they do not invalidate by themselves.
incorrect.C: Sliding expiration extends the lifetime on every access, so entries could outlive 10 minutes.

correct.B: allkeys-lru evicts the least recently used keys when memory is full, keeping the frequently accessed embeddings.

incorrect.A: volatile-ttl only evicts keys that have a TTL, by shortest remaining time, not by usage.
incorrect.C: EXPIRE sets a lifetime on a key; it does not choose which keys stay in memory.
incorrect.D: Time-window expiration is not a Redis eviction policy for keeping hot keys.

correct.B: Strong consistency always shows the latest committed write in every region.
correct.C: Bounded staleness guarantees reads lag writes by at most a set time or number of versions, which is a predictable window.

incorrect.A: Session consistency only guarantees read-your-writes within one session, not across regions.
incorrect.D: Eventual consistency gives no time or version bound.

correct: The monitored container is the source container whose changes are read.
The lease container stores continuation state and partition ownership between runs.
The default change feed mode is 'latest version', which delivers new and updated items.
incorrect: The vector and indexing containers have no role in change feed state.
Full scan and strong consistency are not change feed modes.

correct: PgBouncer is the connection pooler for Azure Database for PostgreSQL and reuses server connections.
Transaction pooling returns the connection to the pool after each transaction, giving the best reuse for high concurrency.
incorrect: Compute scaling, autovacuum and timeout extensions do not pool connections.
Session pooling holds a server connection for the whole session; statement pooling breaks multi-statement transactions; direct mode has no pooling.

correct: A TTL on each key makes AI responses expire exactly after 24 hours.
Deleting related keys when the document changes keeps cached embeddings consistent with the source.
incorrect: Eviction policies and extra memory decide what is removed under pressure, not exact expiry or freshness.
Resetting expiration on every read would extend the lifetime beyond 24 hours.

correct: The embedding field must use the Vector type.
HNSW is an approximate nearest neighbour index with low latency at scale.
incorrect: Numeric and Tag fields cannot be searched by vector similarity.
A flat index does an exact brute-force scan, which does not scale; a metadata index does not index vectors.

correct: CosmosClient is created with the account endpoint and key.
The Database object is where shared throughput is defined.
The Container object performs item create/read/update/delete operations.
incorrect: An indexing policy configures indexing, not any of these three requirements.

correct: 'compositeIndexes' defines a composite index, which is required to ORDER BY more than one property.
The order of each path must match the query (name ascending/descending, city descending).
incorrect: orderBy and sortOrder are not indexing policy keys.
ascending/descending are values for the order of a path, not property names.

correct.B: A pgvector column is the native type that supports vector similarity search.
correct.D: A typed timestamp column allows reliable date filtering and indexing.

incorrect.A: Free-form strings make date comparison unreliable.
incorrect.C: A varchar column cannot be used for vector distance operators.

correct: getContext().getRequest() returns the incoming request so the trigger can read and change its body.
The check handles both a missing tip and a non-numeric/null tip.
setBody(i) writes the modified document back to the request before it is saved.
incorrect: Options that use getResponse, readDocument or request.getValue do not read the request body in a pre-trigger.
setValue and upsert/replaceDocument are not the right way to modify the request body.

correct: Create the CosmosClient first, with endpoint and credentials.
Then specify the database name.
Then get the container reference.
Finally run the query on the container.
incorrect: DatabaseProxy initialisation is not a separate required step in this sequence.

correct: Strong guarantees the most recent committed value is returned.
Bounded staleness lets reads lag by at most one version.
Eventual consistency is acceptable for the final billing record, which is read after all updates have settled.
incorrect: Consistent prefix does not give a one-version lag bound.

correct: count() gives the number of sales.
DateTimeBin(..., 'day', 2) buckets dates into two-day windows, matching ads that change every second day.
Grouping by the same expression gives one row per ad period.
incorrect: max and sum do not count sales.
DateTimePart extracts a date part rather than binning, and the 12-hour bins do not match a two-day ad cycle.

correct: A vector index enables efficient distance calculations between embeddings.
Embeddings are stored as a numeric array in the document.
incorrect: A composite index supports multi-property sorting, not vector search.
Base64 strings cannot be used for vector distance calculations.

correct: WHERE department = 'Finance' filters rows exactly.
ORDER BY embedding <=> :query_embedding LIMIT 5 ranks by distance and returns the top five.
incorrect: ILIKE 'fin%' is a fuzzy match, not an exact filter.
Ordering by created_at ignores similarity.

correct.A: By default every property is indexed. Excluding properties you never query reduces the index work on each write and lowers RU cost.

incorrect.B: Selective indexing of queried properties is nearly the same idea, but the key picks excluding unused properties.
incorrect.C: Changing the partition key does not reduce indexing cost and is a major migration.
incorrect.D: Strong consistency increases cost and does not reduce write RUs.

correct: Capture a baseline first (P95 and EXPLAIN ANALYZE) before changing anything.
Scale to a tier with more memory per vCore so the index fits in RAM.
Re-run the same benchmark to compare P95 and P99 latency.
Review memory pressure and cache hit ratio during peak hours against the baseline.
incorrect: Increasing dimensionality grows the index and worsens the problem.
Disabling autovacuum causes bloat and does not help memory.

correct.B: Absolute expiration (TTL) removes each key a fixed time after creation, regardless of reads.

incorrect.A: allkeys-lru evicts under memory pressure, not after five minutes.
incorrect.C: PERSIST removes the expiry, which is the opposite.
incorrect.D: Sliding expiration resets the timer on access, so frequently read items would never be purged.

correct.A: Invalidating cache entries when the source data changes removes stale data with little management effort.

incorrect.B: LRU eviction frees memory but does not remove stale entries.
incorrect.C: More memory does nothing for staleness.
incorrect.D: Resetting expiration on each read keeps stale items longer.

correct.C: Vector similarity queries need a vector index on the embedding field; a FLAT index enables the search so it returns matches.

incorrect.A: A metadata-only index cannot be used for vector similarity.
incorrect.B: Geo-replication is for availability and does not affect search.

correct: Yes: HSET stores the embedding in a hash field.
No: no search index or vector field schema is created, so similarity search is not enabled.
Yes: expire("doc:1", 600) is 600 seconds, which is 10 minutes.
The change feed processor detects document changes that should trigger vectorization.
More lease container capacity allows scaling out the processing across instances.
incorrect: A periodic full scan or cross-partition query is costly and not event-driven.
Consistency level and RU throughput do not scale out change feed processing.

correct.B: Changing the indexing precision of the vector fields trades accuracy against RU use, which addresses the known issue.
correct.D: Switching to quantizedFlat or diskANN suits large vector sets and reduces RU consumption.

incorrect.A: A composite index does not help vector similarity queries.
incorrect.C: Strong consistency raises RU cost, making the problem worse.

correct: Dynamic concurrency is enabled in host.json.
Of the listed functions, only the queue-triggered function (f3) supports dynamic concurrency.
incorrect: function.json and local.settings.json do not turn on dynamic concurrency for the app.
HTTP (f1) and timer (f2) triggers do not use dynamic concurrency.

correct: Reads can be relaxed per request, so a request can use consistent prefix.
Writes always use the account's default consistency (session), because a per-request override applies only to reads.
incorrect: Strong cannot be requested per request when the account default is weaker.

No: a range filter on the partition key (>) spans partitions, so it is not an in-partition query.
Yes: UserId is not the partition key (/EmployeeId), so the query fans out across partitions.
